equivalent_mutants.reason: The shifted read is inside the zero-result cleanup branch following the direct native-owned 0x4d76e0 parser. Both original 0x4d7793 and the native parser have sole normal return 1. No permitted fixture replaces this owned function. The altered expression therefore cannot execute for any permitted normal-return input, matching the independently reviewed structural coverage exclusion [0x4d613f,0x4d619b).

Changing index < current signed minimum to <= only adds the equality case. Equality of the signed representations implies identical uint32 words; that case writes index back to the same receiver+0x64 word which already holds index. There is no call, aliasing write or callback between the comparison and this store, and no externally observed write trace. All unequal cases retain the same behavior and subsequent maximum handling is unchanged.

limits: Operator new is an emulated allocation service, not the Windows heap.
Operator delete is an emulated release service, not the Windows heap.
The lstrlenA import is supplied by each case using the actual argument string.
InterlockedDecrement is a scripted atomic decrement over the actual CString reference-count word.
Game, MFC collection and CRT string callees execute original instructions on both sides; normal-return comparison does not certify exception unwinding.
FindResourceA supplies native Windows resource availability; the current profile exercises missing embedded bitmap resources through the original filename loader.

The normal-return profile excludes invalid-memory fault parity for nine two-byte allocation-null prefixes; 187 additional bytes are structurally unreachable with the unchanged owned name setter and record parser. All reachable normal-return owned bytes remain required.
notes: Canonical migration retains all 28 previous owners and adds reviewed destructors/cleanup at 0x4ce270, 0x4ce2d0, 0x4d0310, 0x4d6210 and 0x4d6280; legacy native sources remain untouched. Forward-only stdcall wrappers have no proven consumed EAX and retain semantic-void results.
